news.Title: Cognex Q3 Earnings Beat on Strong Demand and Margin Expansion
news.Content:
Cognex Corporation CGNX reported third-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings of 53 cents per share, up 60.6% year over year and 3.92% above the Zacks Consensus Estimate.

Revenues increased 13.2% year over year to $313.39 million, beating the consensus mark by 0.51%. Broad-based factory automation demand, favorable product mix and disciplined cost management supported results. Logistics delivered its 11th consecutive quarter of double-digit revenue growth, while adjusted EBITDA margin expanded significantly.

CGNX Q3 Top-Line Drivers

Third-quarter revenues reached a quarterly record, marking the ninth consecutive quarter of year-over-year growth. Excluding the prior-year commercial partnership benefit, revenues increased 19%. Foreign currency movements did not materially affect consolidated revenues.

Cognex Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Cognex Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Cognex Corporation Quote

Growth was broad-based across major end markets, with Factory Automation strength led by Semiconductor, Packaging and Electronics. Logistics, Packaging, Consumer Electronics and Semiconductor each delivered double-digit revenue growth, excluding currency effects and the divestiture of the Japan-focused trading business.

Automotive revenues increased in the mid-single-digit range. Logistics remained Cognex's largest end market, accounting for 26% of the 2025 revenue mix, followed by Packaging at 21%, Consumer Electronics and Automotive at 19% each, and Semiconductor at 10%.

Cognex Advances AI and Robotics Opportunities

Cognex continued expanding its machine vision capabilities through product innovation and strategic acquisitions. The company announced a definitive agreement to acquire RealSense, a provider of depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and physical artificial intelligence.

The all-cash acquisition is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026. Management believes the transaction will expand its addressable opportunities in robotics and strengthen its position in AI-powered machine vision.

The company also launched the In-Sight 1750, an AI-powered wafer and panel identification system for semiconductor manufacturing. Its advanced optical character recognition technology reads faint or degraded markings, while automated tuning capabilities help reduce setup time.

CGNX's Favorable Mix Boosts Profitability

Gross margin expanded to 70.8% from 67.6% in the year-ago quarter. Adjusted gross margin increased 290 basis points to 71.3%.

Adjusted EBITDA surged 61.8% to $111.4 million. Adjusted operating income increased to $107.1 million from $64.2 million, while adjusted operating margin expanded to 34.2% from 23.2%.

Adjusted EBITDA margin improved 1,060 basis points to 35.5%, marking the ninth consecutive quarter of expansion. Excluding the prior-year commercial partnership benefit, the margin improvement reached 1,340 basis points.

Story Continues

Cognex Maintains Tight Control Over Expenses

Operating expenses decreased 6.6% year over year to $120.9 million. Adjusted operating expenses declined 6.9% year over year to $116.5 million.

Research, development and engineering expenses declined to $33.9 million from $35.1 million. Selling, general and administrative expenses decreased to $87 million from $94.4 million, contributing to improved operating leverage.

CGNX's Balance Sheet and Cash Flow Details

As of Oct. 4, 2026, cash and cash equivalents totaled $694.7 million compared with $262.9 million as of Dec. 31, 2025. Cognex held $846 million in total cash and investments and had no debt.

Net cash provided by operating activities increased to $106.4 million from $87.5 million a year earlier. Free cash flow rose 20.6% to $103.8 million from $86 million. The trailing 12-month free cash flow conversion rate was 106%.

Cognex distributed $14 million in dividends during the quarter.

Cognex Raises Its 2026 Revenue and Earnings Outlook

For the fourth quarter of 2026, Cognex expects revenues between $270 million and $290 million. At the midpoint, this implies 11% growth from reported fourth-quarter 2025 revenues. Adjusted EBITDA margin is projected to be between 29% and 32%.

Adjusted earnings are expected to be between 37 cents and 41 cents per share, representing approximately 44% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. The outlook excludes the pending RealSense acquisition.

For 2026, CGNX raised its revenue guidance to $1.143-$1.163 billion from $1.13-$1.15 billion, indicating 16% growth at the midpoint. Management expects stronger Logistics demand to support the improvement.

The company increased its adjusted EBITDA margin forecast to 31%-32% from 29%-31%, supported by higher revenues and approximately $35 million in targeted annualized net cost reductions.

Adjusted earnings are now projected to be between $1.68 and $1.72 per share, up from the previous range of $1.64-$1.68, implying 67% year-over-year growth at the midpoint.

news.Title: Evercore Names 5 Tech Stocks to Own After Blue Wave
news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Evercore ISI says investors should look beyond the obvious AI winners after Democrats took control of Congress, naming Amphenol, Arista Networks, Apple ( NASDAQ:AAPL ), Cisco ( NASDAQ:CSCO ) and Motorola Solutions as technology stocks that could hold up better in a tougher regulatory environment. Warning! GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Sign with MSFT. Is AAPL fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. The firm's argument starts with data centers. Evercore believes stricter regulation around new projects could weigh on sentiment toward AI infrastructure companies, particularly in states such as Texas, Georgia and Ohio where data-center construction has become a bigger political issue. But the consequences would not be uniformly negative. Slower construction could temper demand for memory products such as DRAM and NAND, potentially easing a major cost headwind for companies including Apple and PC makers. Apple previously said higher memory costs represented roughly a 140-basis-point gross-margin headwind in the December quarter. Evercore called Apple a particularly defensive name because its earnings depend more on iPhone mix, pricing and Services than on new data-center construction. The firm also pointed to resilient demand and the potential for gross-margin recovery. Amphenol offers a different type of protection. Evercore sees the connector maker as a diversified way to retain AI exposure because its business spans high-speed data, power and optical products alongside defense, aerospace and industrial markets. That reduces dependence on any single AI architecture or customer. Arista remains Evercore's preferred high-quality networking exposure, while Cisco could benefit from campus refresh cycles, optics and Silicon One. Motorola Solutions stands apart because its public-safety communications business is less tied to AI spending and more resistant to macro weakness. Investor Takeaway I think the most interesting part of Evercore's call is that a slowdown in AI infrastructure spending does not automatically mean investors should abandon technology altogether . Instead, it may shift the leadership. Companies whose earnings depend directly on ever-rising data-center construction could face more political and permitting risk, while diversified hardware, networking and consumer-tech names may look relatively safer. Apple is probably the clearest example because tighter data-center development could indirectly reduce memory inflation while leaving its core iPhone and Services engine largely untouched. Story Continues For investors, the key things to watch are data-center regulation, memory pricing, Apple gross margins, networking demand and whether capital rotates from pure AI infrastructure plays into more defensive technology names . The election may not end the AI trade. It could change which tech stocks investors want to own. AAPL GF Value chart AAPL GF Value chart The firm's argument starts with data centers.

news.Title: TRMB Q3 Earnings Meet Estimates as AECO Growth Lifts Revenues
news.Content:
Trimble TRMB reported third-quarter 2026 non-GAAP earnings of 86 cents per share, in line with the Zacks Consensus Estimate. Earnings increased 6.2% year over year.

Revenues of $966.8 million increased 7.3% year over year and 7% organically, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 0.09%. Growth was supported by strength in Architecture, Engineering, Construction and Operations (AECO) and Field Systems. Annualized recurring revenue (ARR) reached a record $2.56 billion, increasing 11% year over year and 10% organically.

TRMB's Revenue Mix Reflects Recurring Business Growth

Subscription and services revenues increased 7.3% year over year to $642.5 million, while product revenues advanced 7.2% to $324.3 million. Subscription and services accounted for 66.5% of total revenues, keeping recurring streams central to Trimble's business model.

Management highlighted continued execution of its Connect & Scale strategy, which links physical and digital workflows across construction, geospatial and transportation markets. However, slower ARR growth in Field Systems and Transportation & Logistics tempered overall recurring revenue momentum.

Trimble Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Trimble's AECO Segment Sustains Strong Momentum

AECO revenues reached $395 million, increasing 9% organically. Segment ARR climbed 13% organically to a record $1.636 billion, supported by consistent subscription demand and customer expansion.

Trimble Construction One bundles and cross-selling activity supported bookings growth and stable customer retention. Segment operating income rose 16% to $132.2 million, while operating margin expanded 170 basis points to 33.5%.

Management raised its full-year AECO operating margin expectation to approximately 36%, up 100 basis points from its previous outlook.

TRMB's Field Systems Faces Recurring Revenue Pressure

Field Systems generated revenues of $435.8 million, reflecting 7% organic growth. Demand remained healthy across Civil Construction and Geospatial, particularly from data center construction, utilities, and energy infrastructure.

ARR reached $407 million, increasing 5% organically. Growth moderated due to the transition away from a low-margin white-label product, weaker positioning services demand in South American agriculture and lower-than-expected subscription renewals.

Segment operating income declined 6% to $128.7 million. Operating margin contracted 390 basis points to 29.5%, reflecting product mix, trade show timing and a challenging year-ago comparison.

Story Continues

Trimble's T&L Growth Moderates Amid Freight Weakness

Transportation & Logistics revenues were $136 million, increasing 2% organically. Segment ARR reached $521 million, advancing 5% organically as freight market conditions remained challenging.

Transporeon ARR increased approximately 9% year over year, supported by strong customer retention. However, softer freight volumes and spot pricing weighed on growth. AI-enabled offerings recorded revenue growth exceeding 20% year over year.

Operating income increased 3% to $35.7 million, while operating margin expanded 50 basis points to 26.3%, reflecting continued profitability improvement despite subdued market conditions.

TRMB's Profitability Reflects Hardware Mix Pressure

Non-GAAP gross margin declined 70 basis points year over year to 70.5%.

Adjusted EBITDA rose to $278.5 million from $269.4 million, while the corresponding margin declined 110 basis points to 28.8%.

Non-GAAP operating income increased to $262.6 million from $254.2 million a year earlier. However, non-GAAP operating margin contracted 100 basis points to 27.2%.

Trimble's Cash Flow Supports Continued Buybacks

Trimble ended the quarter with $214.5 million in cash and equivalents and total debt of approximately $1.53 billion. Net debt stood at $1.32 billion, with a leverage ratio of 1.2 times.

During the first three quarters of 2026, operating cash flow reached $664.7 million compared with $225.9 million a year earlier. Free cash flow increased to $643.6 million from $206.2 million.

Share repurchases totaled approximately $224 million during the quarter, leaving $768 million available under the existing authorization.

TRMB Updates 2026 Outlook and Sets Q4 Guidance

Trimble now expects 2026 revenues between $3.91 billion and $3.94 billion and non-GAAP earnings of $3.63-$3.69 per share. The company maintained its revenue guidance midpoint while slightly raising its earnings outlook.

Organic ARR growth is now projected to be approximately 10%, down from the previous expectation of 12%-14%. Non-GAAP operating margin is expected between 28.2% and 28.5%, with adjusted EBITDA margin of 29.8%-30%.

For the fourth quarter, Trimble expects revenues of $1.031-$1.061 billion and non-GAAP earnings of $1.13-$1.19 per share. Organic ARR growth is projected to be approximately 10%, while adjusted EBITDA margin is expected to be between 34.1% and 34.7%.

news.Title: FICO Q4 Earnings Beat on Scores, Pricing and Software Growth
news.Content:
Fair Isaac FICO reported fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 non-GAAP earnings of $11.10 per share, up 43.4% year over year and 2.4% above the Zacks Consensus Estimate.

Revenues increased 27.4% year over year to $657.05 million, surpassing the consensus mark by 0.72%. The quarter benefited from higher mortgage origination Scores pricing and strong software-platform growth, partially offset by weaker mortgage volumes. Software annual recurring revenue (ARR) reached $851 million, up 14% year over year, driven by a 72% increase in platform ARR.

FICO Scores Revenues Rise on Mortgage Pricing

Scores revenues increased 33% year over year to $413.8 million. Business-to-business (B2B) revenues climbed 39% to $356 million, primarily driven by higher mortgage origination score unit prices, partially offset by declining mortgage volumes. Business-to-consumer (B2C) revenues grew 3% to $58 million, reflecting higher royalties from indirect channel partners.

Mortgage origination revenues surged 72% year over year despite volumes declining in the high-single digits amid elevated interest rates. Mortgage originations accounted for 67% of B2B revenues and 58% of total Scores revenues. Auto origination revenues rose 11%, while credit card, personal loan and other origination revenues increased 12%.

Fair Isaac Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Fair Isaac Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Fair Isaac Corporation Quote

Fair Isaac Software Growth Accelerates

Software revenues increased 19% year over year to $243.2 million. SaaS revenues grew 29%, supported by FICO Platform adoption, while on-premises revenues rose 13% due to higher point-in-time revenues. Platform revenues jumped 84%, reflecting customer expansion and migrations, while non-platform revenues declined 12%.

Platform ARR reached $453 million, representing 53% of total software ARR, while non-platform ARR declined 18% to $398 million. Platform dollar-based net retention improved to 156% from 82% for non-platform software, bringing total retention to 112%. The metric measures recurring revenue retained from existing customers, including expansion.

Trailing 12-month software annual contract value bookings increased 36% year over year to $140 million. Quarterly bookings totaled $45 million, marking continued demand for the company's decisioning software.

FICO Expands Scores Distribution and AI Platform

Fair Isaac expanded its mortgage direct licensing agreements to resellers representing approximately 73% of U.S. mortgage volume. The FICO Score 10T Adopter Program reached 84 lenders, representing $684 billion in eligible annual originations and $2.65 trillion in eligible annual servicing.

The company also launched its FICO Preferred Program, offering participating lenders customized mortgage pricing arrangements. Separately, the next-generation FICO Platform and Enterprise Fraud Solution became generally available in October, strengthening its AI-driven decisioning and fraud prevention capabilities.

Story Continues

FICO Margins Expand Despite Higher Expenses

Total operating expenses increased 40.2% year over year to $390.5 million. Research and development expenses rose 1.6% to $51.8 million, while selling, general and administrative expenses increased 79.6% to $225.4 million.

Operating income increased 12.4% year over year to $266.6 million. Non-GAAP operating income reached $402.4 million, while the non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 61% from 54% a year earlier.

Fair Isaac's Cash Flow and Debt Position

As of Sept. 30, 2026, Fair Isaac had $217.6 million in cash and cash equivalents compared with $248.4 million as of June 30, 2026. Total debt stood at approximately $5.26 billion.

Net cash from operating activities increased to $294.2 million from $223.7 million a year earlier. Free cash flow rose to $284.3 million from $210.8 million.

Fair Isaac Withholds Fiscal 2027 Guidance

Management did not provide fiscal 2027 guidance, citing uncertainty surrounding its transition to customized mortgage origination pricing and continued weakness in mortgage market activity.

Elevated interest rates and affordability pressures remain headwinds to origination volumes.

FICO expects to continue negotiating customer-specific pricing programs for calendar 2027. Management also anticipates a significant decline in professional services revenues as it emphasizes strategic partnerships and AI-driven operating efficiencies. They are: leading in smartphone audio, growing our high-performance mixed signal or HPMS content in smartphones and related devices and expanding into new markets and applications. Starting with smartphone audio. This fall, our latest generation custom-boosted amplifier and 22-nanometer smart codec were again featured in newly launched flagship devices and demand for both remained strong through the quarter. Beyond audio performance and power efficiency, these components enable considerable flexibility in system design. History is a good guide to their anticipated longevity. A great example of this is our camera controllers, where we have introduced 3 generations of products since 2020, with each being more capable than the last. Historically, each one has launched in premium models before being designed into a wider range of devices, and we saw exactly that pattern this quarter with a higher attach rate of our third-generation controller in certain models of recently introduced smartphones.

Continuing to execute on our camera road map, we have also now taped out our fourth generation controller, which we expect to enter production in calendar year 2028 and to further increase our content per device. Beyond cameras, we are also seeing good traction in battery and power, where we are continuing the design of our smart power IC for 3D sensing and are in development on a new custom power and battery product. Taking a step back to look at our smartphone business as a whole, we see our content growing in layers with both broader adoption of the parts we already ship and then new components on top of that.

In the near term, over roughly the next 18 months, we expect successive launch windows to bring higher attach rates across a number of our existing ICs. Beyond that, we also expect to build on these gains and further increase our content per device with multiple new components that are now in development, including our fourth-generation camera controller, the smart power IC for 3D sensing and other HPMS components. And we expect continued positive contributions from accessories, wearables and other non-smartphone devices. To reiterate a comment I made in the last call, the pipeline of opportunity across our core audio and HPMS business is among the strongest in the company's recent history.

Moving to our third priority, I'll start with PCs. Since we last spoke, the headwinds we described in this market have not eased. Shortages of memory and other components and the higher prices that follow are weighing on PC demand and market research now points to significant unit declines this year with further pressure on shipments in calendar 2027. In response, OEMs have pushed out some new model launches. And in many cases, those newer models are expected to carry more of our content per system and ship in higher volumes. While that's impacting our near-term outlook, the design wins behind those models are still in place.

We're actively engaged with customers on new programs, and we believe we're positioned for growth as demand recovers. Setting those market dynamics aside, we are seeing tangible evidence of progress in our PC business. In August, I mentioned that several customers plan to ship RTX Spark-based systems with our amplifiers and codecs on board. In October, one of those launched, a new premium PC built on NVIDIA's RTX Spark platform with a 6-speaker audio system powered by Cirrus Logic amplifiers and a codec. It's a great showcase for the, kind of, rich high-fidelity audio we can deliver in thin, power-efficient designs. Audio is one way we're adding value to new PC designs. Voice is another.

And this is an area we are particularly excited about as PCs become increasingly AI-centric. We see a significant opportunity to enable voice as the natural interface for AI-enabled PCs and agentic workflows. Our latest smart codec integrates a dedicated DSP and a low-power wake-up signal chain that handles wake word detection, noise reduction and audio buffering independently of the CPU or NPU. This enables an always-on conversational interaction while simultaneously preserving battery life. Customer interest in this component continued to be strong this quarter. And over time, we expect voice to move from premium platforms into mainstream designs.

Further expanding our product portfolio in this area, during the quarter, we also taped out our second-generation smart codec for AI-enabled PCs, which we expect to sample to customers in the coming calendar year. We also see a growing opportunity in AI gadgets and smart glasses as AI assistants become accessible via new types of wearable and portable devices. These are small battery-powered products that need great voice interfaces, great audio and very efficient power management. And these areas are precisely in our wheelhouse. We're engaged with several market leaders today, and we expect end devices using our products to reach the market in the next few quarters.

In our general market business, I'd like to highlight 2 milestones this quarter. First, as we anticipated in August, we began sampling our new analog front-end components for smart metering. Second, we received the first production orders for our new industrial imaging components. These products are built for high-precision scanning in applications such as line scan machine vision and optical inspection. Instead of piecing together several separate components, customers get one integrated scalable imaging front end, which means improved speed, better efficiency and lower system cost. Customer engagement has been high since we introduced this family earlier this year, and we expect mass production to begin in the December quarter.

Finally, I'm pleased to share that subsequent to the end of the quarter, we completed the acquisition of INVENTVM, a fabless semiconductor company based in Pavia, Italy, that specializes in mixed-signal power management and audio ICs. This is a team we know very well and with whom we've worked closely over the past 5 years. So we've seen their engineering talent and R&D capabilities firsthand. The combined team expands our engineering capacity and strengthens our position and portfolio in the emerging consumer wearable and AI gadget markets that I mentioned earlier. I'd like to extend a warm welcome to the INVENTVM team. And that concludes the latest update on our long-term growth strategy.

So let me now turn the call over to Jeff to provide an overview of our financial results as well as the outlook.

Jeffrey Woolard: Thank you, John. Good afternoon, everyone. I'll now walk through our Q2 financial results and provide guidance for Q3. In Q2 fiscal 2027, we delivered revenue of $559.5 million, which was above the midpoint of our guidance range. Revenue was up 22% sequentially and flat year-over-year. The sequential increase reflects higher smartphone unit volumes and increased content shipping into smartphones and to a lesser extent, growth in custom components in non-smartphone applications. This was partially offset by a decline in PCs and to a lesser extent, a reduction in revenue from certain general market components that are coming to their end of life.

On a year-over-year basis, an increase in smartphone unit volumes and higher content shipping into smartphones was offset by lower general market sales and previously anticipated pricing reductions. Turning to gross profit and gross margin. Non-GAAP gross profit in the September quarter was $300.8 million and non-GAAP gross margin was 53.8%. On a sequential basis, the increase in gross margin reflects lower wafer costs, largely driven by the temporary benefit from wafers purchased under prior agreements with GlobalFoundries that we discussed last quarter as well as lower production ramp expenses. On a year-over-year basis, an increase in gross margin was largely due to a favorable product mix, lower inventory reserves and that same temporary wafer benefit.

This was partially offset by higher freight costs and supply chain costs. Now I'll turn to operating expenses. Our non-GAAP operating expense for the second quarter was $141.6 million. On a sequential basis, OpEx was up $6.2 million, primarily driven by higher product development expenses and variable compensation. Within employee-related expenses, higher salaries from increased headcount were offset by a seasonal reduction in benefit costs. On a year-over-year basis, operating expense was up $13.9 million, primarily due to higher employee-related expenses, product development expenses and R&D development expenses. This was partially offset by lower variable compensation.

These increases are consistent with our previously communicated plan to increase R&D investment in fiscal 2027 to support the range of opportunities across our business. Non-GAAP operating income for the quarter was $159.2 million or 28.5% of revenue. Turning now to taxes. For the September quarter, our non-GAAP tax rate was 17.5%. And lastly, on the P&L, non-GAAP net income was $139.2 million, resulting in earnings per share of $2.70. Let me now turn to the balance sheet. Our balance sheet continues to be strong, and we ended the September quarter with $1.1 billion in cash and investments.

Our ending cash and investments balance was down $90.9 million from the prior quarter as share repurchases more than offset cash generated from operations. We continue to have no debt outstanding. Inventory at the end of the second quarter was $271.2 million, up from $262.7 million in the prior quarter. Days of inventory were down sequentially, and we ended the quarter with approximately 96 days of inventory. Turning to cash flow. Cash flow from operations was $50.9 million in the September quarter and CapEx was $8.6 million, resulting in non-GAAP free cash flow margin of 8%. For the trailing 12-month period, cash flow from operations was $557.3 million and CapEx was $31.7 million.

This resulted in a non-GAAP free cash flow margin of 26%. On share buybacks, in Q2, we utilized $125.5 million to repurchase 991,983 shares of common stock at an average price of $126.51. At the end of Q2 fiscal 2027, the company had $114.1 million remaining on its share repurchase authorization. The Board of Directors recently authorized the company to repurchase up to an additional $500 million of Cirrus Logic common stock. Subsequent to Q2 fiscal year '27, the company utilized $18.6 million to repurchase 170,757 shares at an average price of $108.67 under a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan. Now on to guidance. For Q3 fiscal 2027, we expect revenue in the range of $510 million to $570 million.

GAAP gross margin is expected to range from 51% to 53%. Non-GAAP operating expense is expected to range from $152 million to $158 million. Additionally, as we indicated previously, given the breadth of opportunities ahead of us, we expect our full fiscal year 2027 operating expenses to increase as we invest in R&D. In fiscal 2027, non-GAAP effective tax rate is expected to range from 16% to 18%. Before we turn to Q&A, I'd like to address a number of investor questions that we received in advance of this call related to our October 13 filing on Synaptics. We made acquisition proposals for Synaptics and are not currently pursuing a transaction. We pursued it because the strategic logic was strong.

Pairing our mixed-signal audio and power expertise with Synaptics' connectivity and sensing would have built a broader edge platform and diversified our customer and end market mix. We also went in with a clear view of value, and we held to it. We put forward what we believed was a compelling proposal for Synaptics shareholders that was also right for Cirrus Logic shareholders. When the price moved beyond that, we stepped back. Two things should be clear. First, inorganic growth is a real part of our strategy, and we will keep evaluating opportunities that strengthen our platform and broaden our markets. Second, we will stay disciplined.

Our balance sheet and cash generation give us flexibility, and we intend to use it in ways that create value for our shareholders. Finally, I would also like to note that while we understand there is an intense interest related to our largest customer, in accordance with Cirrus Logic company policy, we will not discuss specifics about our business relationship. With that, let me turn the call over to Chelsea to start the Q&A session.

Chelsea Heffernan: Thanks, Jeff. We will now start the Q&A portion of the earnings call. [Operator Instructions] Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Your first question comes from the line of Tore Svanberg with Stifel.

Cam Tierney: This is Cam Tierney on for Tore Svanberg at Stifel. Yes, I just wanted to ask on INVENTVM a little bit. So I'm curious if their battery management and charging IP feeds into the smartphone road map for your battery IC that you called out in your slide deck? Or is that more focused on non-smartphone markets? And maybe just, kind of, also more broadly, can you talk a little bit about the rationale behind INVENTVM?

John Forsyth: Yes, sure. Thanks for the question. The IP that is in the battery IC we've referred to there in the shareholder letter and the shareholder presentation is based on homegrown IP that we've been developing over the years. So many of the people listening to this call will have heard me say that, that's an area we've been investing in for some time now, and we believe we can offer really differentiated solutions around the battery. So the INVENTVM team is a great team. It's a very high-performing set of engineers, but we didn't go after them for IP in relation to that.

They do have some IP and crucially a lot of expertise around mixed-signal areas that we care a lot about, power management, audio and the like. And it's also a team we know very well, having collaborated with them over the past 5 years. So we do think that their expertise and some of what they've been working on plays very well to another area that I talked about in relation to the emerging category of AI gadgets, AI wearables and so on. And we certainly think they're going to bring a lot to the table for us in that area.

Cam Tierney: All right. And then for my follow-up, I just want to ask, I'm not sure if you guys can answer this, but is there any difference or maybe relative comment that you can make on content for you guys in the Duo versus the 18 Pro iPhones?

John Forsyth: We have seen some teardowns now, I think. So obviously, we got asked this question many times every quarter in advance of the rumored device, and we couldn't say anything. Thankfully, out in the wild, there are teardowns now. So yes, we have 2 audio amps in there, so you can go and see this on the web. We have 2 audio amps, haptics driver, a codec and the amps and the codec are obviously our latest generation products and then 2 camera controllers as well.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Your next question comes from the line of Tom O'Malley with Barclays.

Thomas O'Malley: I had a question on the camera controllers as well. You talked about continued proliferation of the third-generation camera controller, and you talked about the fourth coming in 2028. Is there a road map that you can see that content stepping up as well in the interim period of time? I know that you mentioned too, with the Duo, you've seen even more camera controllers on some phones in the past. Any comments about potential increasing content on that third-generation camera controller?

John Forsyth: Yes. Thanks, Tom. We definitely think there's going to be continued accretion in camera content before we get to the fourth-generation controller, and you got the timing right on the fourth-generation controller there. And that's actually part of a broader attach rate story. So I mentioned this in my prepared remarks, and we touched on it in the letter. But basically, we see -- we have a very positive setup over the next few years, consisting of both growth with content that we have already developed and are shipping today and then new content, which is incremental to what we ship today and then certain introductions like, as you said, newer generations of the camera controller.

So in the camera space, but -- not just in the camera space, actually, across multiple products, we can see opportunity for content attach rates to grow in the coming couple of years. In fact, what I said in the prepared remarks was we look over the next 18 months period, in each of the launch windows within that period, we will see content attach rate growth based on a range of content that we're shipping today. That's not to say attach rate growth ends after 18 months, but it's just to say that in each of those launch windows, we see that as one of the tailwinds to our results.

And then obviously, we have a number of new products in development as well. So the camera controller that you mentioned, we've also talked about the smart IC for sensing, the smart power IC. And then in the prepared remarks and in the shareholder letter, we also alluded to further HPMS content, which is, again, based in the battery and power space, which we've clearly been investing in for some time, and we're delighted to say that we now have another business award in that space, which will represent incremental content in a very high-volume socket as well.

Thomas O'Malley: Super helpful. And then my follow-up is just on gross margin. So we saw the close of -- well, at least the first report of 2 large RF providers. And it looks as though you are seeing some margin pressures into the next calendar year. Obviously, you have a very different relationship with your largest customer, but there are very severe component cost headwinds, and there is pressure, kind of, across the semi universe. So maybe just talk about your ability to keep gross margins at this level with that, kind of, backdrop. Obviously, in the past, like that relationship hasn't worked like that, but there's never been anything this extreme. I would just love to get your view there.

Jeffrey Woolard: Yes, Tom, thanks. Yes, as we mentioned, this was, kind of, a high point for us from a gross margin this quarter, where we're benefiting from some of the wafer prices we had previously. And you can see from our guide, that does drop down from our high point in that 51% to 53%. We see that as far as our foreseeable future, we believe we can be in that range. Now you mentioned it's very tight out there. It is very tight out there. We see that as well. We had also talked about we do have some wafer agreements that give us certainty for price and capacity.

So we do have some insight into what things look like in the future. I think the back end is very tight and something we manage on an almost daily basis to making sure we have capacity and those agreements are, I think, fluid in that part of the supply chain, but we'll continue to manage that. And we will be implementing some targeted price increases across our portfolio. So I think it's a little reckless to go too far out. But as far as we can see, we're comfortable with that 51% to 53% range.

Chelsea Heffernan: And there are no more questions at this time. So I'll turn the call back over to John for final remarks. Actually, sorry. Chris just jumped in the queue.

Operator: And with that, your next question comes from the line of Christopher Rolland with Susquehanna.

Christopher Rolland: Sorry for the late there. I guess a couple for me. First is the decline in September, I think it's fairly rare that you see a decline in the December quarter. Are there -- is there anything else to note there around inventory or build aheads or something affecting seasonality that we should be thinking about there?

Jeffrey Woolard: Yes. Thanks for the question. So if you -- I'm going to, kind of, take you back and look at the full year because I think you have to replay it a little bit to understand the story. But the full year is roughly in line with our expectations where we started the year. And as we talked about, that the shape of the quarter is going to be a little different. That first half is strongly skewed towards premium smartphones, which obviously our content is highest. And if you go back to Q1, if you remember, we were up 3% when we would traditionally have been down 9% in that quarter.

And this was part of that flatter seasonality we discussed. It's just a much heavier content in a heavier Pro mix. Q2 ended up being a little higher. Obviously, we came above the midpoint where that ramp came in a little bit more than we had expected. And so we had more revenue in June and September and some of that December revenue got pulled into September. Also a reminder, when we think about camera content, that shifts a little earlier than the other components. So there really hasn't been a change in demand. It's really a timing issue.

When we look at the March quarter, we see that returning to something that's closer to what we'd see from a normal seasonality, particularly when you bake in PCs have not been meeting our expectations for a lot of the supply chain environment we've talked about on PCs. I think next year, that looks -- not guiding specifically into next year, but I think next year, you'll see that a little bit more traditionally balanced with growth weighted to the second half, where they will also have some content gains and probably will be a tough compare to this year where that first half is just so heavily weighted to the premium phones.

Christopher Rolland: Excellent. Very helpful. My next question, and then I might have one more, believe it or not after that. But you mentioned that you would see content attach rates grow in launches in the next 18 months. I was wondering if there were any other details around type of product or application or anything you can speak about there and maybe even the magnitude of those -- that content growth?

John Forsyth: Yes, Chris, unfortunately, I don't want to say too much, obviously, about customer products. We want to be very respectful of their plans. But as I said, it does extend across multiple product areas for us. So that gives us a very good set of stepping stones of content accretion on our way to the introduction of wholly new incremental sockets that we've also talked about.

Christopher Rolland: Fantastic, John. And last one for me, I promise. Synaptics, this is primarily a digital company, a consumer-based company, overlap both in PC and mobile as well, kind of, similar to you guys. Is this the, kind of, thing that you are interested in going forward on the M&A front? And just, kind of, unpacking your opportunistic, kind of, view of buying them. Is this the, kind of, thing you might be looking for in the future?

John Forsyth: Well, I certainly would say, yes, we're very keen to engage in M&A where we feel that, that can authentically create value for shareholders and enable us to offer something that's really compelling to customers. I think we've been pretty clear that our capital allocation priorities put our organic opportunities first, but M&A is second where we can identify great M&A opportunities. In this case, you've alluded to it that Cirrus has class-leading mixed-signal assets, Synaptics has some solid assets in closely adjacent areas like touch sensing and so on. And there are various places, whether that's PCs or automotive and so on, where we obviously show up very close to each other.

So for example, they do touch and display controllers in cabin. We do haptics in cabin and so on, similar with trackpads and PCs. So we saw a good thesis there and opportunities to build more complete solutions to offer customers. I think there are more -- many more ways than that of creating value at the edge around our technologies. And that's something we obviously think a lot about. And, yes, we will obviously be disciplined with M&A as we have been in this case. We had, as Jeff said, a very clear view of the value.

And we feel very strongly -- strong positive sentiment about our own organic plan and don't want to do anything that puts the value that organic plan is going to create at risk, but we'll continue to look for opportunities for us to grow the offering.

Chelsea Heffernan: Great. And that was our last question. So now I'll turn the call back to John.

John Forsyth: Thank you, Chelsea. So in summary, Cirrus Logic delivered strong results for the September quarter, and we continue to make good progress across each pillar of our long-term strategy. Between the numerous content opportunities that we see in our core business, the products we've just taped out and the progress we're making in new markets, we're very excited about what lies ahead. I'd like to thank all of our employees around the world for their dedication to innovation and to supporting our customers' success. In what remains a challenging supply environment, I also want to recognize our foundry and OSAT partners whose close collaboration and responsiveness have been instrumental in enabling us to meet demand.

And I'd like to express our appreciation to our customers for putting their trust in us and to all of you for your continued interest in our progress. Finally, I'd like to thank everyone for participating today. Goodbye.

Operator: This concludes today's call. Thank you for attending. You may now disconnect.

news.Title: Cisco Systems (CSCO) Reports Next Week: Wall Street Expects Earnings Growth
news.Content:
Cisco Systems (CSCO) is expected to deliver a year-over-year increase in earnings on higher revenues when it reports results for the quarter ended October 2026. This widely-known consensus outlook gives a good sense of the company's earnings picture, but how the actual results compare to these estimates is a powerful factor that could impact its near-term stock price.

The stock might move higher if these key numbers top expectations in the upcoming earnings report, which is expected to be released on November 12. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call, it's worth handicapping the probability of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This seller of routers, switches, software and services is expected to post quarterly earnings of $1.33 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +33%.

Revenues are expected to be $18.09 billion, up 21.5% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 0.12% lower over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that an aggregate change may not always reflect the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. Our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) -- has this insight at its core.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

Story Continues

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.

Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for Cisco?

For Cisco, the Most Accurate Estimate is lower than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bearish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of -0.51%.

On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #2.

So, this combination makes it difficult to conclusively predict that Cisco will beat the consensus EPS estimate.

Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?

While calculating estimates for a company's future earnings, analysts often consider to what extent it has been able to match past consensus estimates. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.

For the last reported quarter, it was expected that Cisco would post earnings of $1.17 per share when it actually produced earnings of $1.22, delivering a surprise of +4.27%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates four times.

Bottom Line

An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.

That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.

Cisco doesn't appear a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, investors should pay attention to other factors too for betting on this stock or staying away from it ahead of its earnings release.

news.Content:
Arista Networks, Inc. ANET reported strong third-quarter 2026 results, with revenues and adjusted earnings soaring year over year, driven by robust demand trends. Quarterly revenues surged 58.5% year over year to $3.66 billion, exceeding the consensus estimate of $3.31 billion by 10.41%. This marked the company's strongest annual revenue growth since its IPO, driven by robust artificial intelligence (AI) networking demand, enterprise expansion and improved supply chain execution. Arista also surpassed 100 Etherlink customers.

On a non-GAAP basis, earnings rose 55.8% year over year to $1.20 per share, beating the consensus estimate of $1.08 by 11.11%. Innovative product launches and steady customer additions backed by the company's best-in-class portfolio strength led to top-line expansion, while steady margin improvement contributed to earnings growth.

ANET Rides on Strong AI Networking Demand

Arista witnessed accelerating demand for its AI networking solutions as customers expanded investments in large-scale AI infrastructure. The company's Ethernet-based networking architecture supports AI training and inference workloads across scale-out and scale-across deployments, enabling efficient connectivity across distributed computing environments.

Arista continues to expand its Etherlink portfolio, comprising at least 25 switches designed for AI networking applications. Management highlighted growing adoption of scale-across networking, which connects computing resources across multiple data centers. It expects this architecture to represent an increasing portion of AI networking deployments in 2027. The company is also advancing rack-scale networking designs through partnerships with leading accelerator providers. Initial scale-up trials are expected in 2027, with production anticipated in 2028.

Portfolio Strength Fuels Growth

Arista offers one of the broadest product lines of data center and campus Ethernet switches and routers in the industry, with industry-leading capacity, low latency, port density and power efficiency. Over the years, the company has introduced various products to meet the rising demands of AI/ML-driven network architectures. These innovations have enabled Arista to deliver a superior customer experience and increase customer engagement.

Arista has expanded its software platform beyond cloud data centers through automation, campus networking, routing and AI networking capabilities. The company's unified EOS (Extensible Operating System) architecture enables programmable networking across client, campus, cloud and AI environments while supporting advanced routing, observability and operational automation.

With customers deploying transformative cloud networking solutions, the company has announced several additions to its multi-cloud and cloud-native software product family with CloudEOS Edge. It has introduced cognitive Wi-Fi software that delivers intelligent application identification, automated troubleshooting and location services. The versatility of Arista's unified software stack across various use cases, including WAN routing and campus and data center infrastructure, has helped it to record steady top-line growth.

Price Performance

Arista has surged 33.2% over the past year against the industry's decline of 3.1%. It has lagged peers like Hewlett Packard Enterprise Company HPE and Cisco Systems, Inc. CSCO. While Hewlett Packard has gained 114.1%, Cisco is up 45.8% over this period.

Earnings estimates for Arista for 2026 and 2027 have increased 25.2% and 30.3%, respectively, to $4.13 and $5.12 over the past year. The uptrend in estimate revisions indicates that investors are bullish about the stock's growth potential.

End Note

With healthy revenue-generating potential driven by robust demand trends, Arista appears poised for solid growth momentum. Further, a strong emphasis on quality, diligent execution of operational plans and continuous portfolio enhancements are driving more value for customers. GlobalFoundries' $21 Billion Deal Could Change the Economics of Chipmaking

Cirrus Logic (NASDAQ:CRUS) reported fiscal second-quarter revenue of $559.5 million, up 22% from the prior quarter, as higher smartphone volumes and increased content per device helped offset weaker PC and general-market sales.

The chipmaker forecast revenue of $510 million to $570 million for the December quarter. Chief Financial Officer Jeff Woolard said some revenue that might have been expected in December was pulled into the September quarter, and that the change reflected timing rather than a shift in demand.

"The full year is roughly in line with our expectations when we started the year," Woolard said. He added that the first half was more heavily weighted toward premium smartphones, where Cirrus has more content per device, and that camera components generally ship earlier than other parts.

Quarterly results and outlook

Revenue for the September quarter was flat from a year earlier and above the midpoint of the company's guidance. Higher smartphone volumes and content were offset year over year by lower general-market sales and previously anticipated price reductions, Woolard said.

Asked about supply-chain cost pressures, Woolard described the September quarter as a high point for gross margin. He said the company has wafer agreements that provide some price and capacity certainty, but backend capacity remains tight. Cirrus plans targeted price increases across its portfolio and is comfortable with a 51% to 53% gross-margin range for the foreseeable future, he said.

Smartphone content and new products

Chief Executive Officer John Forsyth said Cirrus expects adoption of several existing chips to increase across successive smartphone launch windows over roughly the next 18 months. The company also sees opportunities for additional components beyond that period.

Among those products is a fourth-generation camera controller that has completed tape-out and is expected to enter production in calendar 2028. Forsyth said Cirrus also is designing a smart power chip for 3D sensing and developing a custom power and battery product. The company has received another business award in the battery and power area that he said would add content in a high-volume socket.

In response to an analyst's question about the Duo iPhone, Forsyth cited publicly available device teardowns and said the phone contains two Cirrus audio amplifiers, a haptics driver, a codec and two camera controllers.

PC headwinds and market expansion

Forsyth said shortages of memory and other components, along with higher prices, are weighing on PC demand. Some manufacturers have delayed new model launches, including systems expected to carry more Cirrus content and ship in higher volumes. He said the design wins remain in place, though the delays are affecting the near-term outlook.

The company has taped out a second-generation smart codec for AI-enabled PCs and expects to sample it to customers in the coming calendar year. Forsyth also said devices using Cirrus products in AI gadgets and smart glasses are expected to reach the market in the next few quarters.

In industrial markets, Cirrus began sampling analog front-end components for smart meters and received its first production orders for industrial imaging components. Mass production of the imaging products is expected to begin in the December quarter, Forsyth said.

Acquisitions and capital returns

Cirrus completed its acquisition of INVENTVM, a fabless semiconductor company based in Pavia, Italy, after the quarter ended. Forsyth said the deal adds engineering capacity and expertise in power management and audio, particularly for wearables and AI gadgets. He said the company's smartphone battery chip is based on internally developed intellectual property, rather than IP acquired through INVENTVM.

Woolard said Cirrus had made acquisition proposals for Synaptics but is not currently pursuing a transaction after the price moved beyond what Cirrus considered appropriate. He said the company remains interested in acquisitions that broaden its platform and markets, while maintaining price discipline.

Cirrus ended the quarter with $1.1 billion in cash and investments and no debt outstanding. It spent $125.5 million repurchasing shares during the quarter, and its board recently authorized up to an additional $500 million in buybacks.

About Cirrus Logic (NASDAQ:CRUS)

Cirrus Logic, Inc is a fabless semiconductor company that designs high-performance, low-power analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits. Its products are used to process, manage and enhance audio and other signals in electronic devices, including smartphones, tablets, laptops, headphones, smart speakers and automotive systems.

The company's product portfolio includes audio codecs, digital-to-analog and analog-to-digital converters, amplifiers, haptic controllers, sensing solutions and power-management components.

news.Title: STMicroelectronics Unveils STM32A, Edge AI Chips for Automotive and Robotics
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in STMicroelectronics N.V.? Here are five stocks we like better.

STMicroelectronics introduced the STM32A microcontroller family for automotive and high-safety applications, spanning entry-level vehicle nodes through ASIL D-capable zonal endpoints. The lineup is also intended for industrial automation, robotics, energy systems and infrastructure.

ST launched the STM32G5 and STM32H7P microcontrollers for motor control, digital power, signal processing and edge AI. The H7P combines a Cortex-M7 processor, DSP accelerator and 82-GOPS neural accelerator, while the G5 emphasizes higher performance, advanced peripherals and post-quantum security support.

The company expanded its edge-AI strategy through Arm and NVIDIA partnerships, new STM32Cube development tools and updated AI software for model discovery, customization, benchmarking and data preparation. ST also announced STM32Cube for Agentic AI, designed to help coding assistants use STM32-specific development context.

STMicroelectronics Could Reach New Highs—Here's What Needs to Happen

STMicroelectronics (NYSE:STM) used its STM32 Summit in Silicon Valley to outline a "technology convergence" strategy for embedded systems and introduce new microcontroller families and software tools aimed at automotive, industrial automation, robotics, digital power and edge artificial intelligence applications.

The company said its unified STM32 MCU platform is intended to help developers reuse software, tools and intellectual property across product families and markets as systems become more connected, software-defined, security-focused and capable of autonomous operation. ST said the platform is supported by consistent Arm Cortex-M-based architectures, the STM32Cube ecosystem, shared process technologies and a supply chain it manages internally.

According to the company, the STM32 developer ecosystem includes close to 2 million developers, while its ST Community receives more than 300,000 visitors per month. ST also said it has shipped more than 20 billion STM32 devices.

Arm partnership and physical AI

Arm Executive Vice President of the Physical AI Business Unit Drew Henry said ST will be a lead partner in defining the future Cortex-M roadmap, alongside Cadence as a design partner. Henry said Arm has shipped more than 100 billion Cortex-M devices and sees physical AI as a potential $200 billion compute market by the middle of the next decade.

Industrial Chips Are in Rally Mode—5 Ways to Play

"We believe that this is a $200 billion compute market in the middle of next decade or so," Henry said, referring to systems that apply AI to agriculture, manufacturing, transportation and other real-world environments.

ST said it is combining Arm CPUs, its neural accelerators and more than a decade of MCU AI software experience for edge AI workloads. The company also highlighted deterministic Ethernet connectivity, integrated security features including SHA accelerators and post-quantum cryptography libraries, and safety-focused hardware and software support.

STM32A expands into automotive and safety applications

→ Marvell Eyes a Swing for the AI Networking Fences as Markets Weigh Lumentum Price Tag

A central product announcement was the STM32A series, which ST described as a new line combining its general-purpose and automotive microcontroller experience. The series is designed for automotive and high-safety embedded applications, including industrial automation, robotics, energy systems and infrastructure.

ST unveiled the initial three-product roadmap:

STM32A4: Intended for entry-level automotive nodes, including distributed sensing, actuation, doors, windows, lighting and local controls. ST said the devices will offer low cost, compact memory, cryptographic support and LIN implementation.

STM32A5: Targeted at body and comfort-control functions, with up to 4 MB of memory, enhanced security and safety support up to ASIL B. ST said the devices are also suited to mid-range safety-critical industrial, robotics and energy applications.

STM32A9: Intended for higher-function zonal vehicle endpoints, with real-time control, low-latency and Ethernet-oriented connectivity, plus safety support up to ASIL D. ST said its split-lock core architecture can prioritize ASIL D operation or provide twice the ASIL B performance when ASIL D is not required.

The company said the STM32A family will provide continuity with STM32-compatible IP, software concepts, tools and the STM32Cube ecosystem while addressing automotive-grade qualification, functional safety, security and longer product lifecycles.

NVIDIA Vice President of Robotics and Edge AI Deepu Talla discussed the companies' work around robotics and the Holoscan Sensor Bridge, which enables sensor and actuator connectivity over Ethernet. ST said it plans to release Holoscan Sensor Bridge software as a native component of the STM32Cube ecosystem in coming months and intends to develop simulation libraries for its sensor, MEMS, microcontroller and actuation portfolios.

STM32G5 and STM32H7P product launches

ST also launched the STM32G5, a general-purpose mixed-signal microcontroller based on an Arm Cortex-M33 running at up to 280 MHz. The company said the device delivers a CoreMark score more than double that of the STM32G4 and is designed for motor control and digital power applications.

Versions aimed at digital power will include additional high-resolution timers, while motor-control versions will provide more analog peripherals, ST said. Other cited capabilities include a 111-picosecond timer resolution, a position encoder, a programmable logic array with 16 logic elements, a 5-megasample-per-second analog-to-digital converter and pseudo-differential mode for signal-to-noise performance.

The STM32G5 targets SESIP Level 3 and PSA Certified Level 3 security certifications and supports post-quantum cryptographic libraries, according to ST. Initial devices, Nucleo boards and Discovery kits are available, while ST said a dual-core version is being developed for release next year.

Ram Kumar of ST introduced the STM32H7P, describing it as the company's first STM32H7 combining a Cortex-M7 processor, a Hardware Signal Processor DSP accelerator and an 82-GOPS Neural-ART accelerator. The microcontroller operates at up to 520 MHz and delivers a CoreMark score of nearly 2,700, which Kumar said is 150% above most competing solutions.

The STM32H7P includes high-resolution timers, comparators and twice the flash memory of a 1 MB STM32H7 at roughly the same price, according to ST. Kumar said the device is aimed at digital power, digital signal processing and edge AI applications, and can operate in industrial environments up to 105 degrees Celsius through exposed-pad packaging.

AI development software update

ST also updated its AI software offering. Miguel Castro, head of AI marketing and strategy for the Americas, said the company is replacing its Model Zoo interface with Model Explorer, Model Factory and Model Bench tools for discovering, customizing and benchmarking AI models. It also introduced Dataset Factory for organizing and cleaning data.

In addition, ST announced STM32Cube for Agentic AI, a tool intended to provide coding assistants with STM32 documentation, guidelines, examples and other development context. Castro said early experiments reduced token usage by 93% for a blinking-light application, while typical configurations are expected to reduce token usage by roughly 50% to 60%.

STMicroelectronics N.V. (NYSE: STM) is a global semiconductor company that designs, develops, manufactures and markets a broad range of integrated circuits and other semiconductor products. Its offerings support applications in automotive, industrial, personal electronics, communications equipment and computer systems.

The company's product portfolio includes microcontrollers, analog and power semiconductors, sensors, microelectromechanical systems (MEMS), connectivity products and automotive chips.

news.Title: SIMO Earnings Surge as Enterprise and AI Storage Drive New Momentum
news.Content:
Silicon Motion Technology Corporation SIMO delivered a sharp third-quarter earnings acceleration as enterprise, automotive and artificial intelligence storage became larger contributors to growth. The results strengthen the case that its revenue mix is moving beyond traditional consumer storage controllers.

The key question is whether that shift can support a more durable earnings profile. Current guidance, expanding solutions revenue and new enterprise products point to broader growth drivers, though execution and consumer-market risks remain.

SIMO's Third Quarter Set New Financial Highs

Third-quarter 2026 revenues reached $560.2 million, up 131% year over year and 24% sequentially. Non-GAAP earnings of $4.35 per American depositary share beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.30 by 31.82% and increased 335% from the year-ago period.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Profitability also improved materially. Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 32.1% from 15.8% a year earlier, while gross margin rose to 53.7% from 48.7%. The combination of higher volumes and a richer product mix helped lift operating leverage.

Silicon Motion's Solutions Business is Surging

Ferri and boot-drive solution sales climbed 75-80% sequentially in the third quarter, supported by automotive, edge artificial intelligence and enterprise demand. Solutions accounted for more than 40% of total revenues, and management expects the category could represent roughly half of revenues in 2027.

That mix shift could make Silicon Motion less dependent on consumer controller cycles. Automotive programs generally span three to five years, while enterprise boot-drive opportunities provide another source of longer-duration demand. Micron Technology, Inc. MU is also expanding high-capacity data-center solid-state drive offerings for artificial intelligence, cloud and hyperscale workloads, underscoring the broader storage opportunity tied to data-intensive computing.

SIMO's Fourth-Quarter Guidance Extends the Trend

Management expects fourth-quarter revenues of $588 million to $616 million, implying sequential growth of 5%-10%. Non-GAAP gross margin is projected at 54%-55%, while operating margin is expected to reach 36%-37%.

The outlook suggests the third-quarter improvement is carrying into year-end rather than fading immediately after a record period. For 2027, management expects revenue growth of at least 40% and gross margins in the low-to-mid-50% range, supported by rising contributions from enterprise controllers and Ferri automotive solutions.

Story Continues

Silicon Motion Is Building for the Next AI Cycle

Silicon Motion taped out its 4-nanometer PCIe Gen6 MonTitan controller in the third quarter, with sampling scheduled for the first quarter of 2027. The product targets hyperscalers and cloud service providers and is designed for both TLC-based compute storage and QLC-based data storage.

Four NAND makers have begun producing 2-terabit QLC dies, with broader availability expected by the end of 2027. That supply expansion could support higher-capacity enterprise storage deployments. Seagate Technology Holdings plc STX is likewise positioning its mass-capacity storage portfolio around rising artificial intelligence and cloud data demand, showing that infrastructure spending is broadening across storage technologies.

SIMO's Ratings Temper the Earnings Excitement

The latest quarter supports the view that Silicon Motion is becoming a more diversified storage supplier, but the transition is not yet complete. Consumer weakness, customer qualification requirements and supply-chain constraints still create uncertainty around how smoothly the enterprise ramp develops.

SIMO currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). It also has a Value Score of D and Momentum Score of D, along with a Growth Score of F and VGM Score of F. Because the Style Scores complement the Zacks Rank, these weaker grades suggest a more measured near-term stance even as the company's enterprise and artificial intelligence exposure expands. news.Title: SIMO Stock Falls 33.5% in a Month as Growth Meets Execution Risks
news.Content:
Silicon Motion Technology Corporation SIMO shares have fallen 33.5% over the past four weeks, a sharp reversal despite record revenues and expanding exposure to enterprise and AI storage. The drop raises the question of whether valuation now better reflects the company's growth prospects.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The answer is not straightforward. Enterprise diversification, automotive demand and higher-value storage products support the outlook, but consumer weakness, qualification requirements and supply-chain constraints leave execution risk elevated.

SIMO's Record Growth Contrasts With the Sell-Off

Third-quarter 2026 revenues surged 131% year over year to about $560 million, marking a fourth consecutive quarter of record revenues. Non-GAAP earnings per ADS rose 335% to $4.35, while operating margin expanded to 32.1%.

The quarter also exceeded the Zacks Consensus Estimate on both the top and bottom lines. Management expects fourth-quarter revenues of $588-$616 million, with non-GAAP operating margin rising to 36%-37%.

Silicon Motion's Enterprise Mix Is Expanding

Ferri automotive and enterprise boot-drive solutions grew more than 75% sequentially and represented more than 40% of third-quarter revenues. Management indicated that the solutions business could reach roughly half of revenues in 2027.

That shift increases exposure to longer-duration programs and higher-value storage opportunities. Micron Technology, Inc. MU, which offers DRAM, NAND and data-center SSDs, illustrates the broader memory and storage ecosystem in which enterprise demand is expanding.

SIMO Faces Persistent Consumer Pressure

Elevated NAND and DRAM prices are pressuring smartphone and PC affordability. eMMC and UFS controller revenues declined modestly sequentially in the third quarter, and management expects near-term revenues in that business to remain relatively flat.

SSD controller revenues are also expected to be flat to slightly lower sequentially in the fourth quarter. These trends show that enterprise growth is offsetting, rather than eliminating, weakness in established consumer-facing markets.

Silicon Motion Must Execute on Enterprise Ramps

Enterprise expansion depends on customer qualifications, production ramps and component availability. MonTitan is scaling across seven announced customers, while Silicon Motion's 4-nanometer PCIe Gen6 MonTitan controller is scheduled to begin sampling in the first quarter of 2027.

Near-CPU boot-drive opportunities add another execution layer because customized firmware and customer-specific features are required. Seagate Technology Holdings PLC STX, whose portfolio includes cloud, edge and data-center storage products, provides another reference point for the scale and complexity of enterprise storage markets.

Story Continues

SIMO's Valuation Adds Context to the Decline

SIMO trades at 12.1X forward 12-month earnings, below its five-year median of 19.4X but above the Zacks sub-industry's 9.4X. The lower multiple versus its own history reflects a materially different valuation backdrop after the recent share-price pullback.

The discount to SIMO's historical median may look more attractive if enterprise ramps progress as planned. Still, the premium to the sub-industry means investors are not being offered a uniformly cheap valuation relative to peers.

SIMO's Signals Still Favor a Cautious View

SIMO's growth and valuation setup remains mixed. Record operating performance and enterprise diversification support the longer-term case, while consumer pressure and execution requirements argue against treating the 33.5% decline alone as a buy signal.

The stock currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). It has a Value Score of D and Momentum Score of D, along with a Growth Score of F and VGM Score of F. Since the Style Scores are designed to complement the Zacks Rank, these weaker grades support a measured stance despite the company's strong recent fundamental growth.
